title: Microsoft Purview: OCR scans images embedded in Office files and PDFs in SharePoint and OneDrive
summary: The roadmap facts, OCR licensing and meter, and configuration controls are supported. Minor corrections should complete the site-selection route, qualify the estimator guidance, and acknowledge differences in Microsoft's permissions and preview documentation.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans Purview OCR scanning for sensitive information in embedded images in DOCX, PPTX, XLSX and scanned or hybrid PDFs in SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: With Embedded support, OCR will scan content in DOCX, PPTX, XLSX and PDFs (scanned and hybrid containing searchable text and images).

claims.claim: Embedded support is in addition to standalone-image support.
claims.quote: This will be in addition to support for standalone images

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: OCR is optional and requires administrator enablement at tenant level, supporting admin-opt-in rather than an unconditional automatic rollout.
claims.quote: OCR scanning is an optional feature that you must enable at the tenant level.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; summary; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: OCR uses a consumption licensing model through pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: Optical character recognition (OCR) is a pay-as-you-go service that is set up in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: front matter: cost; rationale: cost; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: OCR is metered against an Azure subscription, supporting the variable cost rating.
claims.quote: When you use pay-as-you-go services, you're billed using service meters in the Azure subscription that you specified when you set up pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: Purview OCR location and group settings are reached in Microsoft Purview portal through Settings > Optical character recognition (OCR).
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. Select Settings. Select Optical character recognition (OCR) to enter your OCR configuration settings.

claims.claim: No PowerShell, Graph or other API is documented for the tenant-level Purview OCR location and group settings at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview OCR settings PowerShell Graph API locations groups; Security Compliance OCR Set-PolicyConfig. Read ocr-learn-about, Set-PolicyConfig (no OCR parameter), security-ocrsettings (eDiscovery case only), and Set-SPOTenant (SharePoint sites only).

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The compliance admin configures the tenant's Purview OCR settings.
claims.quote: The Compliance admin for your organization configures the OCR settings for your tenant.

claims.claim: OCR settings generally take effect about an hour after activation.
claims.quote: In general, OCR settings take effect about an hour after you turn them on.

claims.claim: The preview OCR cost estimator is available on the Purview OCR settings page.
claims.quote: Select Settings. Select Optical character recognition (OCR). Under Estimate the cost of an OCR scan for free, select Try for free.

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft 365 admin center site-selection path reaches Edit on the OCR panel.
claims.quote: On the Optical character recognition panel, under Select the SharePoint libraries where you would like to enable optical character recognition, select Edit.
claims.fix: Append ' > Enable optical character recognition in Microsoft 365 > Selected sites (up to 100)' to controls[1].ui.path and its rendered table path. The existing steps are correct but stop before the site-scope setting; the same panel also offers All sites and No sites.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -OpticalCharacterRecognitionSelectedSitesList <String[]> sets the OCR selected-sites list in Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell.
claims.quote:
[-OpticalCharacterRecognitionSelectedSitesList <String[]>]
This parameter allows administrators to pass a list of SharePoint site URLs to modify the optical character recognition premium feature's selected sites list.

claims.claim: The selected-sites parameter requires OCR scope to be SelectedSites.
claims.quote: This parameter can only be called if optical character recognition's scope is set to SelectedSites.

claims.claim: The selected-sites parameter accepts no more than 100 site URLs.
claims.quote: The inputted list of site URLs cannot exceed 100 items.

claims.claim: The selected-sites parameter overwrites the existing list by default.
claims.quote: By default this parameter overwrites the existing list with the user input list.

claims.claim: Using the selected-sites parameter requires pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: Use of this parameter requires that the tenant has pay-as-you-go billing set up.

claims.claim: SharePoint Administrator or Global Administrator is required for the Microsoft 365 admin center OCR setup and site-management surface.
claims.quote: You must be a SharePoint Administrator or Global Administrator to be able to access the Microsoft 365 admin center and set up the OCR service.

claims.claim: The billing subscription is selected through Settings > Org settings > Services > Pay-as-you-go services > Billing > Document processing services > Set up billing and turn on services > Set up billing > Azure subscription.
claims.quote:
On the Services tab, select Pay-as-you-go services.
On the Pay-as-you-go services page, on the Billing tab, select Document processing services.
On the Set up billing and turn on services panel, in the Set up billing section, under Azure subscription, select the dropdown

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell operation is documented for linking this OCR/document-processing billing subscription.
claims.quote: Searched: document processing pay-as-you-go Azure subscription PowerShell Graph API; SharePoint Syntex billing Set-SPOTenant AzureSubscription. Read syntex-azure-billing and pay-as-you-go-setup search excerpts; app/service-prioritization billing results do not document OCR linking.

claims.claim: Billing setup requires SharePoint Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be a SharePoint Administrator or Global Administrator to be able to access the Microsoft 365 admin center and set up the service.

claims.claim: Billing setup requires owner or contributor rights on the Azure subscription.
claims.quote: You must have owner or contributor rights to the Azure subscription that you want to use for pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.fix: Add to the billing permissions sentence: 'The separate Microsoft 365 billing setup page also requires Owner or Contributor rights to the resource group.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/commerce/services/pay-as-you-go-setup, whose Before you begin section says 'You must have Owner or Contributor rights to the Azure subscription and resource group.'

claims.claim: The cited billing page documents disconnecting the subscription, separately from choosing OCR sites.
claims.quote: On the Manage billing panel, under Azure subscription, select Edit billing information. Under Manage billing, select Disconnect Azure subscription.

claims.claim: Tenant OCR settings select scan locations, including SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote:
You can scan images in Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, Windows, and macOS devices.
Select the locations where you want to scan images. Select the groups that you want included or excluded from OCR scans.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Configured OCR extends existing DLP policies to sensitive information in images.
claims.quote: When you configure the OCR settings, Microsoft Purview applies your existing policies for data loss prevention (DLP), records management, and insider risk management (IRM) to images and text-based content.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Configured OCR extends existing records management policies to images.
claims.quote:
SharePoint sites | Data loss prevention Insider risk management Records management: Autoapply retention label policies
OneDrive accounts | Data loss prevention Records management: Autoapply retention label policies

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Configured OCR extends existing insider risk policies to images, with SharePoint listed as a supported location.
claims.quote:
SharePoint sites | Data loss prevention Insider risk management
Considers sensitive information types and trainable classifiers present in images for risk scoring.
claims.fix: Add: 'The insider risk setup page still describes these OCR settings as preview and lists Windows endpoints, SharePoint Online and Teams, not Exchange Online or OneDrive, for that preview.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/insider-risk-management-configure#step-4-recommended-configure-prerequisites-for-policies. The cited general OCR page does not mark these settings preview.

claims.claim: Existing sensitive information types scan images after OCR is configured.
claims.quote: When you enable OCR, all sensitive information types and trainable classifiers can detect characters that are in images.

claims.claim: Existing trainable classifiers scan images after OCR is configured.
claims.quote: When you enable OCR, all sensitive information types and trainable classifiers can detect characters that are in images.

claims.claim: Existing exact data match sensitive information types scan images after OCR is configured.
claims.quote: Once OCR is configured, existing sensitive information types, exact data match based sensitive information types, trainable classifiers, and fingerprint SITs scan images as well as documents and emails.

claims.claim: Existing fingerprint sensitive information types scan images after OCR is configured.
claims.quote: Once OCR is configured, existing sensitive information types, exact data match based sensitive information types, trainable classifiers, and fingerprint SITs scan images as well as documents and emails.

claims.claim: Learn already lists embedded DOCX, PPTX and XLSX images and scanned or hybrid PDFs as supported in SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: SharePoint and OneDrive | ... PDFs (scanned and hybrid containing searchable text and images) Embedded images in DOCX, PPTX, XLSX

claims.claim: Learn states that normal OCR scanning covers images uploaded after OCR is enabled; the briefing separately explains backfill.
claims.quote: Only images uploaded after OCR is enabled are scanned.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Text extracted from images in Office files is indexed for search.
claims.quote: Any images added to these files will be automatically scanned using OCR, and the extracted text will be indexed for search purposes and integrated into compliance solutions.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Text extracted from images in Office files is integrated into compliance solutions.
claims.quote: Any images added to these files will be automatically scanned using OCR, and the extracted text will be indexed for search purposes and integrated into compliance solutions.

claims.claim: The minimum image resolution is 50 x 50 pixels.
claims.quote: Image resolution | 50 × 50 px minimum, 16,000 × 16,000 px maximum

claims.claim: The maximum image resolution is 16,000 x 16,000 pixels.
claims.quote: Image resolution | 50 × 50 px minimum, 16,000 × 16,000 px maximum

claims.claim: The SharePoint and OneDrive OCR file-size maximum is 50 MB.
claims.quote: File size (SharePoint, OneDrive, Windows, and macOS endpoints) | 50 MB max

claims.claim: OCR extracts only the first 2 million characters.
claims.quote: OCR extracts only the first 2 million characters of text.

claims.claim: The SharePoint OCR service supports hub sites and the primary site of a site collection.
claims.quote: This service is available only for SharePoint sites - including hub sites, sites associated to a hub site, and the primary site of a site collection.

claims.claim: Subsites are unsupported.
claims.quote: Subsites aren't supported.

claims.claim: OCR's recognition function extracts text, with policy responses supplied by existing compliance policies.
claims.quote: The optical character recognition (OCR) service in SharePoint lets you extract printed or handwritten text from images and documents.

claims.claim: Start-SPOSiteOpticalCharacterRecognitionBackfill starts a SharePoint OCR backfill job.
claims.quote: Initiates a job to trigger the OCR process for all files for the selected site.

claims.claim: Backfill processes files that have never been OCR processed.
claims.quote: This cmdlet starts a job to trigger the OCR process for files that have either never been OCR processed or have been modified since the last OCR process.

claims.claim: Backfill also processes files modified since the last OCR process.
claims.quote: This cmdlet starts a job to trigger the OCR process for files that have either never been OCR processed or have been modified since the last OCR process.

claims.claim: Running the backfill cmdlet incurs cost.
claims.quote: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is a pay-as-you-go feature. Running this cmdlet will incur cost for your organization.

claims.claim: Backfill cannot be cancelled once triggered.
claims.quote: Once the cmdlet is triggered, the backfilling process cannot be stopped. Disabling OCR on the selected site will not cancel the ongoing backfilling session.

claims.claim: Microsoft refers readers to Adobe requirements for using Purview DLP features with PDFs.
claims.quote: For information about the Adobe requirements for using Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) features with PDF files, see this article from Adobe: Microsoft Purview Information Protection Support in Acrobat.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Licence
claims.claim: After Syntex billing information is entered, the compliance admin can configure Purview OCR without extra setup or licensing requirements.
claims.quote: After you enter billing information in Microsoft Syntex, your Compliance admin can configure OCR in Microsoft Purview without any extra setup or licensing requirements.

claims.claim: Any tenant user can use these document-processing services provided they have a Microsoft 365 licence.
claims.quote: Organization-wide access: Any user in your tenant can use the services, provided they have a Microsoft 365 license.

claims.claim: Using Purview OCR does not require setting up Microsoft Syntex itself.
claims.quote: To use OCR, set up Microsoft Syntex pay-as-you-go billing. (You don't need to set up Microsoft Syntex itself.)

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The published OCR rate is $0.001 per transaction in USD.
claims.quote:
What's billed? (USD)
Optical character recognition | ... | $0.001/transaction

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing: Meter
claims.claim: Each scanned image counts as one OCR transaction.
claims.quote: Each image scanned counts as one transaction.

claims.claim: Each page in a PDF is charged separately.
claims.quote: It also means that each page in a PDF file is charged separately.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; Open questions
claims.claim: The pricing row counts PDF, TIF and TIFF pages and embedded images in Teams chats and email.
claims.quote: the number of pages processed for PDF, TIF, or TIFF; or the number of embedded images in Teams chats and email messages. Each of these counts as one transaction. Processing occurs every time the file is edited.

claims.claim: Embedded images are not rescanned when only file text is updated.
claims.quote: However, in embedded file types, if only text is updated, images aren't scanned again.

claims.claim: SharePoint de-duplicates images to avoid duplicate charges.
claims.quote: SharePoint has implemented de-duplication processes to check for unique images to avoid duplicate charges against the same images.

claims.claim: A scanned image can be used in any number of DLP, insider risk, auto-labeling and records management policies at no extra charge.
claims.quote: Additionally, you can use each scanned image in any number of policies across data loss prevention, insider risk management, auto-labeling, and records management at no extra charge.

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go charges can be monitored in Microsoft Cost Management for Azure.
claims.quote: You can monitor your pay-as-you-go usage in Microsoft Cost Management for Azure.

claims.quote: Through June 2026, if you have pay-as-you-go billing set up, your organization receives a limited amount of included capacity each month for selected services, letting you try these services at no cost.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Estimating; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The preview OCR cost estimator projects costs before OCR is enabled.
claims.quote: The tool scans your selected locations ... and projects how much OCR processing will cost before you enable it.
claims.fix: Qualify the estimator checklist sentence with: 'Use it only before OCR is enabled and if your tenant has not already used its one-time estimation opportunity; OCR and the estimator cannot run simultaneously, and the estimator cannot be re-enabled.' These restrictions are in the cited estimator page's Limitations section.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Estimating; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The estimator does not support embedded images in SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote:
Estimation for embedded images in SharePoint and OneDrive is not supported yet.
Estimation of images in pdf files isn't supported in SharePoint and OneDrive. As a result, your actual OCR bill for SharePoint and OneDrive may be higher than estimated

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Not yet published; Open questions
claims.claim: No separate rate or specifically identified meter line is published for embedded Office-file images in SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint OneDrive Office embedded images OCR pricing meter transaction DOCX PPTX XLSX. Read syntex-pay-as-you-go-services, ocr-learn-about and ocr-overview. They publish a general OCR transaction rate, but no separate Office-embedded rate or named meter line.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No OCR spending cap is documented; selecting sites or a billing subscription is not itself a monetary cap.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview SharePoint OneDrive OCR spending cap limit stop charges budget. Read syntex-azure-billing, syntex-pay-as-you-go-services, ocr, ocr-learn-about and tutorial-acm-create-budgets. Found scope controls and alerts, not an OCR monetary cutoff.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Not yet published
claims.claim: Azure subscription budgets can monitor spending on the subscription used for OCR.
claims.quote:
You can create an Azure subscription budget for a monthly, quarterly, or annual period.
Notifications are triggered when the budget thresholds are exceeded. Resources aren't affected, and your consumption isn't stopped.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Linking pay-as-you-go enables OCR on all SharePoint sites by default.
claims.quote: After an Azure subscription is linked to pay-as-you-go, OCR will be automatically set up and enabled for all SharePoint sites.

claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive OCR supports BMP, PNG, JPEG, GIF, TIFF, HEIC and many raw-camera formats.

claims.claim: OCR supports more than 150 languages.
claims.quote: OCR scanning supports more than 150 languages.

claims.claim: The document-processing licensing page does not state availability for GCC High or DoD.
claims.quote: Searched: GCC High and DoD in the complete syntex-licensing page read this run. Its government-cloud note names GCC only; neither GCC High nor DoD appears.

claims.claim: The SharePoint OCR scope setting offers All sites, Selected sites (up to 100), and No sites.
claims.quote: On the Enable optical character recognition in Microsoft 365 panel, change the setting from All sites to Selected sites (up to 100) or No sites.

claims.claim: If service and DLP site selections differ, the maximum number of sites is enabled for OCR.
claims.quote: The compliance admin can specify which SharePoint sites to include for data loss prevention. If there are different sites specified for the service and data loss prevention, the maximum number of sites will be enabled for OCR.

claims.claim: Using both service and DLP OCR site settings does not charge twice for processing.
claims.quote: You won't be charged twice for processing.
